## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible walk1 math kernel combined with a simple non-Halide walk2 (RNG-order scatter) can still approach the streaming ceiling via compiler vectorization of the math path.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p FALLS from 12.219 at N=4000 to 8.538 at N=16000 — overhead amortization well past the L1d spill (N≈963). Cost then stays FLAT through the L2 spill (N≈61680): 8.343 at N=65000, 8.373 at N=262000, rising only mildly to 8.78 at N=4000000. There is no knee at the L2→DRAM transition. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.05 plateaus near 9.0–9.1 ns/p, q=0.25 near 11.3–11.5 ns/p. The N-shape is invariant across death rates — only the floor shifts up with churn.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.15 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — 32% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. At q=0.05 the peak falls to 7.53 GB/s (30%), at q=0.25 to 6.03 GB/s (24%). The cell is overhead/compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound: it never approaches the ceiling at any N or death rate. Higher death rate monotonically lowers achieved bandwidth, but even at the lowest churn the gap to ceiling is large. No transition to bandwidth-bound behavior occurs.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize — the histogram shows 0 vector-suffixed instructions. All floating-point work is scalar: `fmul s`, `fadd s`, `fsub s`, `fcvtzs` operate on single 32-bit lanes. The walk1 math is offloaded to `_halide_b2_math` via `bl`, but the walk2 scatter loop is entirely scalar with byte-granular accesses: 16 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` instructions write/read individual RGB bytes, with `csel`/`ccmp`/`tbnz` branches for bounds checking on every pixel. The sole `ldr q0` at entry loads a constant, not vectorized data. Byte-granular scatter and scalar arithmetic explain why bandwidth stalls at 32% of ceiling — neither loads nor stores can stream, and per-particle branch overhead dominates.

## Verdict
Refuted — the cell never exceeds 8.15 GB/s (32% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate. The compiler emitted 0 vector instructions; all math is scalar `fmul s`/`fadd s` and the walk2 scatter uses byte-granular `strb`/`ldrb` with per-particle bounds-check branches. The Halide-expressible walk1 path did not yield vectorization, and the non-Halide walk2 scatter caps bandwidth far below ceiling regardless of churn.
